_comment: jobs/backbone_screen MODE=qwen36_a3b: backbone scout. STOCK Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B@995ad96e (35.95B params in the checkpoint incl. vision tower + MTP head, both skipped: ~34.7B text = ~64.6 GiB bf16; hybrid 30 Gated-DeltaNet + 10 gated-attention layers, 256 experts / 8 active + shared expert, ~3B active; NOT attention-free) on the 644 proxy600 rows, frozen scorer. Question: is this backbone stronger than Qwen3.5-9B for the decision task before an attention-free conversion? Two arms in ONE model load (jobs/backbone_screen/arms.py): (a) m0 = the stock Qwen3.5-9B readout of job-5cmat (jrt-chatml-v1 options-first JRT prompt, chat template with empty think block, sum log p(' ' + id + terminator), option-count temperature) and (b) v3w-generic (make_v3w('qwen3.6-35b-a3b'): own chat template with enable_thinking=False, own single-token code table, word ids; identity pinned). Paired b - a and each vs stock RWKV7 v3w (27.32). One H100 80 GB, bf16, transformers 5.17.0 (qwen3_5_moe -> Qwen3_5MoeForCausalLM, experts grouped_mm); fork KV budget 131,072 token-rows, m0 fork_max_rows 32. Precedent job-76vfb (QRWKV6-32B, two arms, two loads): 26 min. Quote 90 x $0.063 = $5.67; worst case (60 + 2 x 90) x 0.0495 = $11.88.
